etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: First attested in 1615; borrowed from Latin discrīminātus, perfect passive participle of discrīminō (“to divide, separate, distinguish”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from discrīmen (“a space between, division, separation, distinction”), from discernō (“to divide, separate, distinguish, discern”). By surface analysis, dis- +‎ criminate.
senses: To treat or affect differently, depending on differences in traits.
Having its differences marked; distinguished by certain tokens.
